concerns: The proposed contrast overstates the national preference: Indonesian speakers also commonly use "jalan terus" for continuing straight.
response.cue_rationale: Both answers express continuing without turning.
material_concerns: "Jalan terus" is an ordinary same-sense Indonesian alternative, so presenting "jalan lurus" versus "jalan terus" as a clear national contrast may mislead learners.

preference_risk.rationale: "Jalan terus" is plausibly ordinary for this same direction sense in both Indonesian and Malaysian Malay.

response.rationale: Both forms fit "go straight," but the claimed Indonesian–Malaysian distinction is too strong because "jalan terus" is also common in Indonesian directions.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: "Jalan terus" is also ordinary Indonesian for going straight, while "jalan lurus" is understandable and usable in Malaysian Malay; everyday usage can therefore defeat the proposed preference.
